summary: Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist who taught Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as President of Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.

Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under V. P. Upadhyaya. He founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation and held posts as Reader (attested 1973) and Professor (attested 1991) at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. She completed her MA, PhD, and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, later serving as Professor, Faculty Dean, and Emerita at the University of Bern.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Allahabad, Lincoln's Inn, and Oxford. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta in 1917 and President of the Numismatic Society of India in 1928.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an archaeologist and Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, the Government of India as Officiating Government Epigraphist (~1930–1932), and the Archaeological Survey of India as Deputy Director-General (1937–1944).

Indologist Kashinath Trimbak Telang studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone College (~1868–1872), President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1889–1893), and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1892–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist who taught Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla and Masaaki Hattori. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1945–1976).

Kasten Anders Rönnow was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his master's at Uppsala University and studied under Jarl Charpentier. He held acting professorships at Uppsala University in 1928 and Lund University in 1932–1933.

Katarzyna Marciniak is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Her career includes posts at the University of Warsaw as a postdoctoral researcher in the Research Centre of Buddhist Studies (attested 2016) and as an adjunct (2020).

Kate Crosby, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Oxford, Hamburg, and Kelaniya. She held posts at Cardiff, SOAS, and King's College London before becoming Professor of Buddhist Studies at Oxford in 2022.

Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London by 2008. She was affiliated with Birkbeck, University of London, as attested in 2010.

Katharina Sabernig specializes in Tibetology. She earned an MD from the Medical University of Vienna (1997–2008) and a PhD from the University of Vienna (2007–2017), and has held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katharine von Garnier-Moewes was an Indologist and linguist. She pursued her studies at the University of Leipzig and Heidelberg University, where she earned a PhD around 1904–1907.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at McGill University, where she earned a Master of Arts under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann, alongside instruction from teachers including Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Chicago and a PhD at McGill University. She was a Professor at McGill University from around 1978 to 2014.

Kathleen D. Morrison is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She served as Assistant Professor at Northwestern University (~1993–1996) and became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2017.

Kathleen Gough was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed her Ph.D. at Girton College, Cambridge. She held academic posts at Brandeis, Oregon, Simon Fraser, and the University of British Columbia.

Kathleen Higgins is a philosopher who received her Ph.D. from Yale University. She became a professor at the University of Texas at Austin in 1992 and held visiting fellowships at Bellagio Center, the Australian National University, and Canberra School of Music.
